validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real. 'Dominion Gas Pipeline' (GEM's row name) is not how any source names an entity -- but 'Dominion Transmission, Inc.' certainly existed and is well documented. DUPLICATE evidence, strongest finding on this row: SEC filing Eastern Gas Transmission & Storage, Inc. 10-K exhibit 3.1 (Certificate of Amendment, filed 2022, CIK 0001936737, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1936737/000119312522189499/d365547dex31.htm) is the corporate charter history of this exact entity and documents, in order: 'CNG Transmission Corporation' amended April 2000 -> 'Dominion Transmission, Inc.' (named as the surviving corporation in a Dec 31, 2001 certificate of merger) -> renamed 'Dominion Energy Transmission, Inc.' effective May 12, 2017 -> renamed 'Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.' effective Nov 2, 2020. Independently, Berkshire Hathaway Energy Co's FY2020 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1081316/000108131621000011/bhe-20201231.htm) states BHE acquired '100% of the equity interests of Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. ("EGTS") (formerly known as Dominion Energy Transmission, Inc.)' in the Nov 2020 GT&S Transaction, and that EGTS's own pipeline/storage operations sit in 'Maryland, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia.' P0176's GEM values (Owner1='Dominion Energy' 100%, StartLocation naming Maryland/Ohio/Virginia, network-scale length 6,059 km, status=operating) describe exactly this same corporate lineage, one name-era behind P3220's current corporate name (Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage System). Both P0176 and P3220 are recorded as network/system-scale rows (blank SegmentName, thousand-plus-mile lengths, blank or single-state termini) rather than discrete route segments -- the same granularity problem the Sweep SOP already flags for P0169 Columbia Gas Transmission. I could not find a source distinguishing a genuinely separate physical scope for the two rows (e.g. one being transmission-only and the other transmission+storage+gathering) -- the ~380 km length gap (6,059 vs 6,437.38) and ~2,300 MMcf/d capacity gap (7,200 vs 9,500) look like different snapshot years/sources of the same evolving system, not two different pipelines. Recommend Baird/an update pass adjudicate: either merge/retire P0176 into P3220 with genealogy noted, or if GEM intends P0176 as a deliberate historical/legacy entity (pre-2020 corporate era) it needs a non-operating status and a note explaining the split -- an 'operating' status on BOTH names as of a 2023-08-11 LastUpdated (three years after the rename) is very likely double-counting one system. I did not attempt the merge myself -- this is a scope/identity call, not a mechanical fix.

validity.researcher_notes: Confirmed the scar: the gem.wiki-sourced Wikipedia stub 'Dominion Transmission' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_Transmission, last edited 2020, no citations of its own) describes the system as bringing gas 'into New England' -- so GEM's original (uncorrupted) value was almost certainly the region name 'New England,' later mangled to 'New United Kingdom.' But 'New England' is not itself a usable state/province value (it appears zero times elsewhere in either tracker per the batch brief), and more importantly the CURRENT, sourced operating footprint of this system does not extend into any New England state at all: BHE's FY2020 10-K states EGTS's (this entity's successor name) transmission/storage pipelines sit in 'Maryland, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia' -- New York is the northeasternmost point. My read is that the Wikipedia stub's 'into New England' phrasing describes gas flowing onward past Dominion's own pipe via interconnecting pipelines (Algonquin/Iroquois/Tennessee Gas at the NY state line), not that this pipeline's own facilities are sited in a New England state. Proposing New York as the best-supported specific terminus state. This is corroborated by two independent-enough sources (the SEC 10-K's explicit state list, and the Wikipedia stub's storage-fields-in-PA/WV-plus-flow-toward-New-England description, which is consistent with a New York handoff point) but neither source names a specific New York location for this system's terminus, so I'm marking this medium tier rather than high -- treat as the best-evidenced correction, not a pinpoint-verified endpoint. Alternative reading: since this is a network/system-scale row (like P0169's blank StartState convention), leaving EndState/Province blank rather than any single state may be the more honest network-level treatment -- flagging both options for the researcher who applies this.
